701749.t: Apparently from ἄριστος (ắrĭstos, “best”) + -τερος (-teros, “contrastive suffix”), though the left direction has negative connotations in many cultures and languages, including Greece.

701753.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ayerīston, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eyeri-h₁d-to-. First part in ἦρι (êri, “early”), second is zero-grade of ἔδω (édō, “to eat”), thus “early meal”.

701736.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂er-dʰrom, from *h₂er- (“to fit”) + *-dʰrom (“tool or instrument suffix”), synchronically analyzable as ἀραρίσκω (ararískō) + -θρον (-thron).

701766.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *árktos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ŕ̥tḱos (“bear”). Cognates include Latin ursus, Welsh arth, Sanskrit ऋक्ष (ṛ́kṣa), Old Armenian արջ (arǰ), and Albanian ari.

701778.t: Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂(e)rmós, from the root *h₂er- (“to fit together, join”), whence also ἀραρίσκω (ararískō, “join, fit together”).

701776.t: From *ἁρμων (*harmōn) + -ία (-ía). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂er- (“to join, fit, fix together”).

701775.t: From Proto-Hellenic *armód͏̌d͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂er- (“to join, fit, fix together”).

701711.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *árguros. Further from a u-stem of Proto-Indo-European *h₂erǵ- (“white; argent”).

701765.t: Utimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂erk- (“to protect, guard, hold, contain”).

701789.t: From ἀρόω (ăróō, “I plow”) + -τήρ (-tḗr, masculine agent noun suffix). See also ἄροτρον (árotron).

701764.t: Unclear. Has been derived from ἄρκυς (ắrkŭs, “net”).

701731.t: From Proto-Hellenic *warḗn, from Proto-Indo-European *wr̥h₁ḗn (“lamb”). Cognates include Latin vervēx (“wether”), Sanskrit उर॑ण (úraṇa) and Old Armenian գառն (gaṙn).

701727.t: Apparently from a Proto-Indo-European *h₂rh₁téh₂, from a root *h₂erh₁- (“to arrange, fit”).

701744.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂ri-dʰh₁-mó-s, from *h₂rey- (“to count, arrange”). Cognates include Old Irish rím, Old English rīm (English rhyme), and perhaps Latin rītus.

701704.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *h₂erǵ- Proto-Indo-European *-rós Proto-Indo-European *h₂r̥ǵrós Ancient Greek *ἀργρός (*ărgrós) Ancient Greek ἀργός Dissimilated from an earlier *ἀργρός (*argrós), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂r̥ǵ-ró-s, from *h₂erǵ-…

701792.t: From Proto-Hellenic *árotron, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂érh₃trom, from *h₂erh₃- + *-trom; equivalent to ἀρόω (aróō, “to plough”) + -τρον (-tron, instrument noun suffix).

701754.t: Probably from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éristos (“fittest, most fitting, most suitable”), the superlative of *h₂er- (“to fit, be suitable”).

701781.t: According to the LIV, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂r̥-né-s-ti, from *h₂res- (“to refuse, deny”).

701768.t: From Proto-Hellenic *árhmə, inherited in turn from Proto-Indo-European *h₂érsmn̥, from *h₂er- (“to fit together, join”), the same source as ἁρμός (harmós, “join”) and ἀραρίσκω (ararískō, “join, fit together”); cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀀𐀗 (a-mo /⁠arhmo⁠/).

701716.t: Contracted from ἀέρδην (aérdēn), from the root of ἀείρω (aeírō, “to lift”) + -δην (-dēn, deverbal adverb suffix).

701722.t: According to Beekes, possibly from a disyllabic Proto-Indo-European root *h₂erh₁- (“to please, satisfy”), which appears to be related to *h₂reh₁- (“to think, reason, arrange”), apparently reanalyzed from *h₂réh₁(ye)ti, a stative-durative verbal form from…

701798.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ároura, from the Proto-Indo-European heteroclitic noun *h₂érh₃-wr̥ ~ *h₂r̥h₃-wén-s, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂erh₃-.

701709.t: From ἄργυρος (ắrgŭros, “silver”) + κόπτω (kóptō, “to strike; to cut”).

701728.t: According to Beekes, from a Proto-Indo-European *h₂reh₁ǵ- (“to help, support”). Cognates include Proto-Germanic *rōkijaną (“to take care of”).

701750.t: From ἀριστεύς (aristeús, the best man, the bravest man) + -εύω (-eúō, suffix forming denominative verbs).

701748.t: From ἀριστεύω (aristeúō, “to be best”) + -εία (-eía, abstract noun suffix).
